purpose: Replay the exact phase-3 shifted-query plans through LeRobot's torchcodec decoder path and compare each batch with pyav. Backend-comparison evidence only: no detector, threshold, severity, score, README, causes.json, board or history change, and no dataset patch, dtype shim or loader monkey-patch.
experiment: direct decoder: upstream decode_video_frames(path, frozen phase-3 plan queries, tolerance_s=1e-4, backend='torchcodec'), with a same-process pyav control; LeRobotDataset not constructed
query_plan_reuse: Every batch of each phase-3 plan file is replayed in file order, with its exact video_query_s values, cameras, anchors, configs, clamped rows and is_pad flags. No query is regenerated, added, dropped or re-selected. common.load_phase3_plan refuses a plan whose sha256 differs from the phase-3 preregistration.

backends.torchcodec: lerobot.datasets.video_utils.decode_video_frames(path, queries, 1e-4, 'torchcodec'), the release's own decode_video_frames_torchcodec. 0.3.3 builds VideoDecoder(path, device='cpu', seek_mode='approximate') per call; 0.4.0 reuses a module-level VideoDecoderCache keyed by path, opened through fsspec. Both are left as shipped.
backends.pyav_control: decode_video_frames(path, queries, 1e-4, 'pyav') in the same process and environment, interleaved per batch. It is recorded separately and never replaces the frozen phase-3 pyav evidence.
backends.default_backend: decode_video_frames(path, [first query], 1e-4, None) is attempted once per case after all batches. get_safe_default_codec() is recorded before batches. The result is recorded, never substituted.

boundary_treatment: Unchanged from the phase-3 plans. Loader-derived padded batches repeat the clamped boundary row's timestamp with is_pad=true. nominal_grid queries are unclamped single calls flagged outside_episode by the phase-3 rule.

outcome_classes.tolerance_error: AssertionError containing 'violate the tolerance' (LeRobot's check, the same assertion in both backends).
outcome_classes.index_error: torchcodec RuntimeError containing 'Invalid frame index' (validateFrameIndex). Query-caused: the lookup is rejected before the tolerance check.
outcome_classes.end_of_stream_error: torchcodec error containing 'no more frames left to decode'. Query-caused.
outcome_classes.dependency_error: 'Could not load libtorchcodec'. Infrastructure, not evidence.
outcome_classes.harness_discrepancy: The independent replay did not reproduce the upstream outcome or output tensor. Not evidence.

decision_rules.buckets: loader_derived/in_range, loader_derived/padded, nominal_grid/in_range and nominal_grid/outside_episode are evaluated separately per backend and never pooled across buckets, backends, cases or releases.
decision_rules.bucket_verdict: tcmodel.bucket_verdict: supports_claim if any batch has a query-caused rejection (tolerance_error, index_error or end_of_stream_error), with 'via' naming the mechanisms; contradicts_claim if every batch ran and returned frames; unresolved if no rejection and any batch hit dependency_error, other_error, harness_discrepancy or did not run; not_applicable if empty.
decision_rules.case_classification: As in phase 3: the torchcodec 'shifted loader-derived lookup' verdict merges loader_derived/in_range and loader_derived/padded, mapped supports_claim->confirmed, contradicts_claim->refuted, unresolved->unresolved. The in_range and padded verdicts are also reported separately. nominal_grid buckets are a labeled comparator and never count as evidence for or against a claim.
decision_rules.mechanism_disclosure: When a confirmation rests on index_error or end_of_stream_error and not on tolerance_error, the report says so. The FineART assertion names tolerance_s, so a FineART confirmation via index validation would not be reported as a tolerance confirmation.
decision_rules.identity: Any preregistered-file, phase-3 plan, input, upstream-source, package-set or torchcodec-environment mismatch stops the case: no batch runs and it stays unresolved.
decision_rules.infrastructure: If torchcodec cannot load in an environment, every case there is unresolved (dependency), not passed or failed.

comparison_rules.per_batch: Same outcome class for torchcodec vs the pyav control, and torchcodec vs the frozen phase-3 pyav outcome.
comparison_rules.returned_timestamps: Per query, the pts of the frame each backend returns (torchcodec: frame at the argmin position over the batch's loaded pts, as upstream; pyav: the window frame at the argmin). Converted to integer ticks of the stream time base and compared exactly. When a torchcodec batch is rejected, the per-query own-index frame pts from the replay is compared and labeled as replay-only.
comparison_rules.tensors: Pixel equality is claimed only from the same-process pyav control, because phase 3 kept no tensors or hashes. Per query when both backends return frames: exact uint8 equality, else max/mean absolute difference and the fraction of differing values.
comparison_rules.pixel_difference_investigation: Differing pixels with equal pts are not called wrong-frame selection. For each such query, the torchcodec frame is also compared with pyav frames at window offsets -2..+2 and the closest offset is reported. Wrong-frame selection is reported only where returned pts differ. Colour-conversion paths differ by source: torchcodec 0.5 CpuDeviceInterface uses swscale SWS_BILINEAR to RGB24 when width % 32 == 0, else a filtergraph 'scale=W:H:sws_flags=bilinear'; torchvision 0.22.1 VideoReader pyav uses PyAV frame.to_rgb().
comparison_rules.control_vs_phase3: The pyav control's per-batch outcome and per-query returned pts are compared with the frozen phase-3 evidence. Any difference is reported as control drift, and the phase-3 evidence is left unchanged.

predictions.rule: tcmodel.predict_batch on demuxed packet pts with r_frame_rate, nb_frames and time base from the container header. Written before execution and hashed in preregistration.json.
predictions.use: Tests the reading of the torchcodec source against the installed binary. Disagreements are reported. They never change a verdict.

limits: Direct-decoder results only. They never establish LeRobotDataset, DataLoader or training behaviour.
Decoding is not semantic frame-to-row alignment. FineART's declared 30 fps vs observed 90 Hz and droid's row/video alignment question stay separate and untested here.
One episode per case, four anchors, default policy configs from phase 3. Untested episodes are not validated.

Releases 0.3.3 (droid, r94) and 0.4.0 (FineART) only; 0.5.1 and other torchcodec/FFmpeg builds are untested. The FFmpeg used is PyAV 15.1.0's bundled 7.1.x build; a system or conda FFmpeg 7 may decode pixels differently.
No severity cutoff, product certification or aggregate accuracy figure is derived.
